necessary_context.content: An opaque handle retains one independently drawn scalar sample loss forever. Requesting a handle gives no observation and is free. Each gradient or complete-Hessian evaluation costs one; both derivatives at one point cost two, and a same-sample endpoint difference costs two evaluations of that derivative. Arbitrary adaptive revisits and unqueried outputs are permitted; computation is free.
necessary_context.name: Reusable-sample derivative oracle

necessary_context.content: Assumptions 1–5 impose a finite initial gap, uniform sample gradient/Hessian Lipschitzness, unbiased derivatives, almost-sure uniform derivative-noise bounds and a globally bounded population gradient. An (epsilon,gamma)-SOSP has gradient norm <=epsilon and minimum Hessian eigenvalue >=-gamma, with per-instance success probability >=2/3.
necessary_context.name: Admissibility and SOSP

necessary_context.content: Upper bounds hold for every finite dimension with logarithmic dimension dependence. Matching lower bounds require sufficiently large dimension growing with inverse tolerances; no dimension-independent supremum over arbitrary dimension or fixed-small-d matching statement is made.
necessary_context.locator: Section 3.1 p.7; Theorem 4.2 and Corollary 1 p.9
